newsitem.title: USA: BPA delays curbs on AC Pacific Intertie to weekend.
newsitem.headline: BPA delays curbs on AC Pacific Intertie to weekend.

text.p: Maintenance work scheduled today and Tuesday on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie has been delayed until Saturday and Sunday, the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Monday.

BPA, which operates the the 4,800 megawatt (MW) line running from the U.S. Northwest to California, said it is currently operating at 3,200 MW, the level it has been limited to since an August 10 power outage.

The line had been scheduled to reduce north to south transmissions to 2,000 MW today and Tuesday during heavy load hours so that San Francisco-based Pacific Gas & Electric Co (PG&E) could carry out line maintenance.
But a trade source at PG&E said the work has been delayed due to warmer-than-expected weather in northern California.
A source at BPA's transmission group said plans to restrict the AC line on Wednesday through Friday to 2,800 MW during heavy load hours remain in place.
In addition, the agency has received verbal notification to reduce the line's capacity to 2,900 MW on Tuesday, but this has not been confirmed in writing.
